title: Master Numbers 11, 22 and 33: Meaning in Chaldean Numerology
description: What are master numbers 11, 22 and 33? See how Chaldean numerology reads them, where they appear in your chart, and what each one asks of you.
keywords: master numbers, master numbers numerology, master number 11 22 33, what are master numbers, chaldean master numbers
h1: Master Numbers 11, 22 and 33 · Read Through the Chaldean Lens
intro: Master numbers are 11, 22 and 33, numbers made of a repeated digit that many numerologists leave unreduced because of their intensity. Western (Pythagorean) numerology gives them a special status. Chaldean numerology reads them as compound numbers with their own meaning, and then reduces them: 11 to 2, 22 to 4 and 33 to 6. This page explains both views and links to each number in depth.

sections.h2: Do master numbers exist in Chaldean numerology?
sections.html: Not as a separate category. Cheiro and the Chaldean tradition give every number from 10 to 52 its own compound meaning, and 11, 22 and 33 are part of that series. What Western sites call master energy, Chaldean numerology describes through the compound and the planet of the digit it reduces to. In practice the two readings point the same way: these are intense, high-potential numbers with a steep learning curve.

• Birthday: born on the 11th or 22nd (no month has a 33rd).
  • Life Path: your full date of birth adds to 11, 22 or 33 before reducing.
  • Name: the Chaldean letter values of your name total 11, 22 or 33.

The free analysis shows your Birth Number, Life Path and Name Number, and the compounds behind them.

faq.a: 11, 22 and 33. Western numerology leaves them unreduced. Chaldean numerology reads them as compounds that reduce to 2, 4 and 6.

faq.q: Is having a master number rare?
faq.a: Fairly common for 11 and 22 through birthdays and names, and less common for 33, which can only appear through life path or name totals.

faq.q: Is a master number better than other numbers?
faq.a: No. It is more intense, not better. Each master number brings strong gifts and a demanding growth theme.
Some modern sites include 44, but the traditional list is 11, 22 and 33. In Chaldean numerology 44 is simply another compound number.
